prompt: After a release, some users still see the old page layout, and a hard refresh fixes it for them.
tells: some users still see the old page layout
why: Browsers or the CDN still hold old assets. Use content-hashed filenames and purge the CDN.
trap: Rolling back won't help users who are still on the old version.

prompt: A product's price was corrected in the database 20 minutes ago, but the API still returns the old price for some requests.
tells: corrected in the database 20 minutes ago
why: A cache layer (Redis, app memory, CDN) wasn't invalidated on update. Invalidate on write or lower the TTL.
trap: "Some requests" can point to one bad host, but the DB is correct, so look at what sits in front of it.

prompt: After updating a feature setting, requests alternate between the old and new behavior depending on which app server answers.
tells: alternate between the old and new behavior
depending on which app server answers
why: Each server caches settings in memory with its own expiry. Broadcast invalidation or use a shared cache.
trap: It looks like config drift, but the servers will converge on their own once their caches expire.

prompt: A user who just signed up gets "account not found" for five minutes, then everything works.
tells: for five minutes, then everything works
why: An earlier lookup cached "not found" (a negative cache entry) with a 5-minute TTL.
trap: Replication lag fixes itself in seconds; a clean five minutes points to a TTL.
